newsitem.title: USA: Perot attacks Clinton for ethical lapses.
newsitem.headline: Perot attacks Clinton for ethical lapses.

text.p: Reform Party presidential candidate Ross Perot attacked President Bill Clinton for ethical lapses, corrupt campaign financing and a lax attitude toward illegal drug use during a speech on Saturday.

"I promise you this; if you elect me as your president I will put a sign up that this White House is not for sale at any price, at any time," Perot told an enthusiastic crowd of about 900 supporters during a rally in a working class suburb south of Detroit.

Perot mentioned Bob Dole, the Republican Party candidate, only in passing. He spent much of his time criticising Clinton for what he called illegal fund-raising tactics. The Democratic Party has recently come under fire for what some say are questionable money-raising practices.

Perot also went after Clinton for refusing Perot's invitation to appear on a paid television programme with him to answer questions on whether he plans to pardon people who have gone to prison because of the Whitewater trials.
"I don't think in the history of politics anybody has offered to throw a million dollars on the table to let another person defend his integrity," he said.

It was the second time the Texas billionaire has stopped in Detroit during the 1996 presidential campaign. The first time, in early September, Perot spoke to the the Economic Club of Detroit and used his remarks to outline his economic plans.

On Saturday, conscious of the blue-collar union workers who live in Detroit, Perot warned of the dangers of exporting jobs overseas, the trade imbalance with China and the growth of low-paying jobs in the United States.
Aware that organised labour traditionally supports Democrats, Perot, who once sat on the board of General Motors Corp, told the crowd: "I don't care about your money. I care about your vote."
Perot's speech, which lasted for nearly 90 minutes at the Allen Park Municipal Auditorium, was the seventh stop in a cross-country campaign swing Perot has been on since Wednesday, Oct. 30.
Perot planned to return to Dallas on Saturday night and spend Sunday taping political infomercials that will air Nov. 4, the night before the election.
The infomercials will be shown for one hour on ABC from 8-9 p.m. EST; on NBC from 8-8:30 p.m. EST; and on CBS from 8:30-9 p.m. EST.
